rationale: A wins because it knows where the facts stop: `Pitching "near a model 4x its size" as established fact would be a fabrication` is exactly the guardrail this update needs. B has good instincts, but it turns `runs offline` into `a quiet challenge to the cloud-inference business every major AI lab depends on`, which is a whole market thesis not in the update. The difference is discipline, not polish.
gaps_in_A: `Hugging Face gives the model away and charges $50 a seat for the audit logs` shrinks the paid tier too much; the update says private model hosting, SSO, and audit logs, not just logs.

`Why a Fortune 100 manufacturer signed on early for private model hosting` slightly overstates the known fact; the update says it is an early enterprise customer, not which enterprise feature made it sign.
`24hr — standard launch news` on the artifact angle is a bit too perishable; downloadable open weights can support testing follow-ups beyond day one if the proof lands.
gaps_in_B: `a quiet challenge to the cloud-inference business every major AI lab depends on` invents a competitive economics story the update does not supply. That belongs in a reported analysis after cost, latency, and market proof, not in the angle set as fact.

`Hugging Face's new open model never has to leave the building — which is exactly the point for security-conscious buyers` infers a security/compliance buyer story without a supplied regulated customer or deployment fact.

`A Fortune 100 manufacturer just became an early customer for Hugging Face's offline AI model` is the serious miss: the update says an early enterprise hub customer, not an offline-model or on-device-AI customer.

`two of the five angles... hinge entirely on an unverified, self-reported number` is a useful warning, but B still keeps the benchmark-dependent competitive-threat angle alive instead of refusing or quarantining it.
